subject: Staggered renewal structure and ops credit for Medicore renewal
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — staggered buckets + ops credit

Hi Allyson / Samir,

Thanks again for the time last week. We reviewed Medicore's last 6 months of usage (attached) and put together a renewal structure that matches how your teams are onboarding new models while keeping unit economics predictable. High-level proposal attached (Proposed_Staggered_Pricing_v3.pdf).

Key points: 
- Staggered quarterly buckets instead of one large annual uplift (Q1 small bump, Q2+ progressive increases)
- 18% operational onboarding credit applied to Q1 invoice to offset migration and spike costs
- Co-term to Dec 31, 2027 (to align with your fiscal cycle)
- Option to convert unused quota in Q1 into a one-time credit for Q2 (escape hatch)

Could you confirm the procurement timeline you need and whether a one-quarter ops credit + staged buckets would be acceptable as a counter to the 30% up-front discount you mentioned? If helpful I can loop in finance/legal to accelerate an amendment.

Attachments: Medicore_MonthlyUsage_202605-202610.csv (usage), Proposed_Staggered_Pricing_v3.pdf (proposal)

Thanks,

Evelyn — thanks for the proposal and the usage file. A few quick clarifications from procurement's side: 

1) Our core ask is minimizing upfront cash impact while giving the Commercial teams confidence on unit pricing. A one-quarter ops credit is interesting, but procurement prefers a fee-structured concession (i.e., a 30% reduction applied to the first quarter invoice).
2) How does the staggered bucket plan handle overages? We need auto-fallback to the prior contracted rate with clear caps — procurement won't agree to open-ended exposure.
3) We will need legal amendments and a PO window of 45 days from signature.

If you can share a numeric example (what an invoice would look like under your staged model versus a straight 30% Q1 discount), that will help expedite internal review.

Best,

Team — forwarding Medicore's reply. Quick take and options for signoff: 

Context: Medicore wants to reduce upfront cash friction (prefers a 30% Q1 invoice reduction). Allyson is open to alternatives if we show concrete invoice math and firm overage protections.

Options we can propose (ranked):
- Option A (recommended): 18% ops credit applied to Q1, staggered quarterly bucket increases (15% increase each quarter), capped overage rate = current contracted rate + 10%. Convert unused Q1 bucket to credit for Q2.
- Option B: 30% straight Q1 discount, but require a minimum uplift commitment across the year (higher annualized commit).
- Option C: 0% discount; provide a one-time implementation credit + longer co-term (2.25 yrs) and favorable SLAs.

Requests: 
- Karthik: run the revenue/ARR and unit economics comparison for Option A vs Option B (attach back numbers) — we need the effective ARR change and margin impact.
- Jordan: can you draft a short amendment template we can send to Medicore if they accept Option A? Need PO timing and signature window language.
- Irene: confirm whether CS can accept the convert-unused-bucket flow operationally and document the handoff checklist.

I attached Proposed_Staggered_Pricing_v3.pdf for reference. Aim: reply to Allyson with a concrete numeric example within 24 hours.

Thanks,
Ben

Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion — staggered buckets + ops credit (numbers)

Ben / team — ran the models for Option A vs Option B. Summary (high level):

- Baseline (no concession): annualized committed uplift = $1,200,000; expected ARR impact = +$1.1M after expected churn/overage patterns.
- Option A (18% Q1 ops credit + staged increases): effective first-year revenue = $1,050,000 (net of credit); annualized ARR impact = +$980k; margin neutral after expected usage smoothing.
- Option B (30% Q1 discount all-up): effective first-year revenue = $930,000; annualized ARR impact = +$840k; materially worse on margin and reduces up-front cash by ~17%.

Recommendation: Offer Option A (18% ops credit) with two guardrails: 1) capped overage rate (current contracted rate + 10%), 2) convert-unused-Q1-to-credit clause limited to 50% of Q1 bucket. This preserves a credible revenue profile while meeting procurement's cash-smoothing ask.

I've attached a CSV with month-by-month invoice sketches (Medicore_MonthlyUsage_202605-202610.csv) and embedded a short sample invoice in the proposal PDF. If legal agrees to a 45-day PO window, cash timing is acceptable.

Happy to join the client call to walk the numbers tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final counter — staged buckets + 18% Q1 ops credit (request to sign)

Allyson / Procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal review, here is our final counter-proposal: 

1) Staged quarterly buckets: Q1 = baseline + 12% uplift, Q2 = Q1 + 15%, Q3 = Q2 + 15% (see attached PDF for numeric example).
2) One-time operational onboarding credit: 18% applied to Q1 invoice (to address migration and spike costs).
3) Overage protection: overage rate capped at current contracted rate + 10%; automatic notifications at 75% and 90% utilization.
4) Convert-unused-Q1: up to 50% of unused Q1 bucket can be rolled forward as a credit into Q2.
5) Co-term to Dec 31, 2027; 45-day PO window from signature.

Please see the Proposed_Staggered_Pricing_v3.pdf attached for the sample invoice and math. If this is acceptable we will share a short amendment and DocuSign link. Our ask: sign the amendment by Oct 28 to lock in the structure and ensure go-live support for your teams.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If you prefer a numeric bill example first, happy to generate a side-by-side invoice comparison for Option A vs a straight 30% Q1 discount — but our recommendation remains Option A to protect long-term unit economics.
